questions: Should the function treat characters other than '(' and ')' as errors, ignore them, or assume they never appear?
If a group has mismatched parentheses (e.g., more '(' than ')'), should it raise an error, return a partial depth, or assume balanced input?
Does the function need to handle leading/trailing spaces beyond those separating groups, or multiple spaces between groups?
Is the input guaranteed to have at least one group, or should it handle empty string input (return empty list)?
Should the depth counting start at 0 (no parentheses) or 1 (first opening parenthesis)?
Are groups defined strictly by spaces, or could other whitespace (tabs, newlines) separate groups?
If a group is empty after splitting (e.g., consecutive spaces), should it be ignored or cause an error?
Should the function validate that each group ends with depth 0 (balanced) before returning max depth?
